title: Psalms Chapter 60 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 60 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 60 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 60.

questions.question: Who is the psalmist mentioned in Psalms 60:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 states that this psalm is a Michtam of David.

questions.question: In Psalms 60:1, whom did Joab smite in the valley of salt?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 says Joab smote Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:2, what has God made the earth do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:2 states, 'Thou hast made the earth to tremble'.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:2 ask God to heal?
questions.explanation: The verse asks God to 'heal the breaches thereof'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:3, what has God made the people drink?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:3 says, 'thou hast made us to drink the wine of astonishment.'

questions.question: What has God given to those who fear Him, according to Psalms 60:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:4 says, 'Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee'.

questions.question: Why is the banner given to those who fear God displayed, according to Psalms 60:4?
questions.explanation: The verse states the banner 'may be displayed because of the truth'.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:1 refers to a battle involving Aramnaharaim and Aramzobah.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 says David strove with Aramnaharaim and Aramzobah.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:2 says the earth is stable and unshaken.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:2 says the earth 'trembleth' and 'shaketh', so it is not stable.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 60:3, God has shown His people easy things.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:3 says God has shown His people hard things, not easy things.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:4 ends with the word 'Selah'.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:4 ends with 'Selah'.

questions.question: In Psalms 60, which comes first?
options: God giving a banner to those who fear Him
God making the people drink the wine of astonishment
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 mentions Joab smiting Edom before other events described in verses 2-4.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:1, what has God done to His people?
options: Cast them off and scattered them
Made them victorious over all foes
questions.correctAnswer: Cast them off and scattered them
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 says, 'O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us'.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:2, why should God heal the breaches?
options: Because the city is under attack
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:2 says, 'heal the breaches thereof; for it shaketh.'

questions.question: In Psalms 60:3, what does the psalmist say God has shown His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:3 says, 'Thou hast shewed thy people hard things.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 60 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 60 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:5, what is the believer asking God to do for His beloved?
options: Deliver and save with His right hand
questions.correctAnswer: Deliver and save with His right hand
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:5 explicitly asks God to deliver His beloved and save with His right hand, highlighting reliance on God's saving power.

questions.question: How does Psalms 60:6 describe God's declaration about Shechem and the valley of Succoth?
options: God will divide Shechem and mete out the valley of Succoth
God will destroy Shechem and burn Succoth
God will bless Shechem and Succoth with peace
God will abandon Shechem and Succoth
questions.correctAnswer: God will divide Shechem and mete out the valley of Succoth
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows God's promise to divide Shechem and measure the valley of Succoth, indicating divine allocation and control over the land.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:7 reveal about the relationship between God and the tribes Gilead, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Judah?
options: God claims ownership and leadership over these tribes
God distances Himself from these tribes
God punishes these tribes for disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God claims ownership and leadership over these tribes
questions.explanation: The verse states 'Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim also is the strength of mine head; Judah is my lawgiver,' showing God’s ownership and governance.

questions.question: What symbolic action does God declare concerning Moab and Edom in Psalms 60:8?
options: Moab is His washpot; He will cast His shoe over Edom
Moab will be blessed; Edom will be honored
Moab will be destroyed; Edom will be ignored
Moab and Edom will be allies
questions.correctAnswer: Moab is His washpot; He will cast His shoe over Edom
questions.explanation: Verse 8 uses symbolic imagery to show God's authority and judgment over Moab and Edom.

questions.question: How does Psalms 60:5–6 together teach about trusting God's promises during hardship?
options: They show that God will deliver and grant victory over adversaries
They encourage self-reliance without God's help
They warn believers to avoid conflict altogether
They suggest God is indifferent to our struggles
questions.correctAnswer: They show that God will deliver and grant victory over adversaries
questions.explanation: Verse 5 asks for deliverance and saving power, while verse 6 affirms God's holy promise to divide the land, encouraging trust in His deliverance and justice.

questions.question: If a believer is struggling with feeling abandoned by God, how does Psalms 60:5 provide hope?
options: By reminding that God’s beloved will be delivered and saved
By stating that God ignores those in trouble
By advising to give up and seek help elsewhere
questions.correctAnswer: By reminding that God’s beloved will be delivered and saved
questions.explanation: Verse 5 reassures believers that God’s beloved are delivered and saved, encouraging faith even in times of despair.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:7, what role does Judah play in relation to the other tribes?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 specifically calls Judah 'my lawgiver,' indicating its leadership role in law and governance.

questions.question: What virtue does Psalms 60:12 emphasize about the source of true courage and victory?
options: Trusting God enables us to do valiantly
Relying on human strength is sufficient
Victory depends on military might alone
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God enables us to do valiantly
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that through God we shall do valiantly, showing that courage and victory come from reliance on God, not human power.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:8 invites Philistia to triumph because of God's power.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says 'Philistia, triumph thou because of me,' indicating God invites Philistia to rejoice in His victory.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Moab is my washpot' in Psalms 60:8 suggest about Moab's status?
options: Moab is considered lowly and subject to God's authority
Moab is an equal ally with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Moab is considered lowly and subject to God's authority
questions.explanation: The washpot was a lowly item in ancient times, so calling Moab a washpot symbolizes its subjugation under God's authority (verse 8).

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:6 and 60:7, how does God show His sovereignty over the land and tribes?
options: By dividing territories and claiming tribes as His own
By abandoning the land and tribes
By allowing the enemy to control the land
questions.correctAnswer: By dividing territories and claiming tribes as His own
questions.explanation: Verse 6 speaks of dividing land, and verse 7 claims tribes as God's possession, showing His control and sovereignty.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:11 expresses confidence that human help is sufficient in times of trouble.
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says 'for vain is the help of man,' showing human help alone is insufficient; divine help is necessary.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:5 teach about the importance of prayer in difficult times?
options: Prayer is a call for God’s deliverance and attentive hearing
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is a call for God’s deliverance and attentive hearing
questions.explanation: Verse 5 asks God to save and hear the speaker, emphasizing prayer as a vital means to seek God's help in trouble.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:9 questions who can lead the psalmist into Edom, implying reliance on God’s guidance.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 asks, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' highlighting the need for divine guidance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:10 reveal about the psalmist’s perception of God’s presence in battle?
options: God had cast them off and did not go with their armies
God guaranteed victory without any effort
God was irrelevant to their military success
questions.correctAnswer: God had cast them off and did not go with their armies
questions.explanation: Verse 10 laments that God had cast them off and did not go out with their armies, expressing a feeling of divine absence.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 60 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 60.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:9, what is the psalmist asking about the strong city and Edom?
options: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who will lead me into Edom?
Who will destroy the strong city? Who will conquer Edom?
Who will build the strong city? Who will bless Edom?
Who will abandon the strong city? Who will forsake Edom?
questions.correctAnswer: Who will bring me into the strong city? Who will lead me into Edom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:9 explicitly asks 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' indicating a request for guidance into these strategic places.

questions.question: In Psalms 60:10, what is the psalmist's tone when addressing God after being cast off?
options: A plea for God to return and lead the armies
A declaration of God’s abandonment and rejection
A celebration of God’s constant presence
A command for God to punish the enemies
questions.correctAnswer: A plea for God to return and lead the armies
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:10 shows the psalmist asking 'Wilt not thou, O God, which hadst cast us off? and thou, O God, which didst not go out with our armies?' indicating a plea for God's return and leadership.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:11 indicate about human help compared to divine help?
options: Human help is vain; help must come from God
Human help is sufficient and reliable
Human help is better than divine help
Human help and divine help are equal
questions.correctAnswer: Human help is vain; help must come from God
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states 'Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.' emphasizing that human help is ineffective without God’s intervention.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:12, by whose power will the people do valiantly and tread down enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:12 says 'Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies,' attributing victory entirely to God’s power.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase "Moab is my washpot" in Psalms 60:8?
options: It symbolizes Moab’s lowly status and subjugation
It praises Moab as a place of cleansing
It refers to a Moabite religious ritual
It indicates Moab’s strength and independence
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes Moab’s lowly status and subjugation
questions.explanation: In Psalms 60:8, calling Moab a 'washpot' uses a metaphor for something lowly or used for washing feet, indicating Moab’s subjugated status culturally and politically.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes Psalms 60:12's theme of divine empowerment for victory?
options: Exodus 15:6 - "Thy right hand, O LORD, is become glorious in power"
Genesis 1:1 - "In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth"
Proverbs 3:5 - "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart"
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 15:6 - "Thy right hand, O LORD, is become glorious in power"
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:6 celebrates God's powerful right hand defeating enemies, paralleling Psalms 60:12 where victory is attributed to God’s power.

questions.question: How does Psalms 60:6 describe God’s promise regarding Shechem and the valley of Succoth?
options: God will divide Shechem and mete out the valley of Succoth
God will destroy Shechem and abandon Succoth
God will bless Shechem and protect Succoth
God will ignore Shechem and the valley of Succoth
questions.correctAnswer: God will divide Shechem and mete out the valley of Succoth
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:6 states 'I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem, and mete out the valley of Succoth' indicating God’s sovereign allocation of these lands.

questions.question: What literary device is present in the structure of Psalms 60:1 which begins and ends with the theme of rejection and plea for restoration?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 frames the psalm with 'O God, thou hast cast us off... O turn thyself to us again,' creating an inclusio that brackets the theme of rejection and restoration.

questions.question: In Psalms 60:7, which tribe is described as the 'lawgiver'?
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states 'Judah is my lawgiver,' assigning the role of lawgiver specifically to the tribe of Judah.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'banner' in Psalms 60:4 likely symbolize?
options: A visible sign of protection and rallying for those who fear God
questions.correctAnswer: A visible sign of protection and rallying for those who fear God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'banner' (nes) in Psalms 60:4 symbolizes a standard or rallying sign displayed to the faithful as a sign of truth and protection.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:11 states that help from man is effective and reliable.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:11 says 'for vain is the help of man,' indicating human help is ineffective, so the statement is false.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of divine strength enabling believers to overcome enemies, similar to Psalms 60:12?
options: Romans 8:37 - "In all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us"
John 3:16 - "For God so loved the world"
Hebrews 11:1 - "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for"
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:37 - "In all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us"
questions.explanation: Romans 8:37 echoes Psalms 60:12’s theme by affirming believers overcome enemies through divine power and love.

questions.question: What historical context is reflected in Psalms 60:1's mention of Joab smiting Edom in the valley of salt?
options: Military conflicts between Israel and Edom during David’s reign
questions.correctAnswer: Military conflicts between Israel and Edom during David’s reign
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 references Joab’s military campaign against Edom, reflecting the historical conflicts during King David’s reign.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 60:3 indicates that God has shown the people pleasant and easy things.
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:3 states 'Thou hast shewed thy people hard things: thou hast made us to drink the wine of astonishment,' indicating difficult experiences rather than pleasant ones.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a passage that thematically connects with Psalms 60:10's plea for God's presence in battle?
options: Exodus 17:11 - Moses holding up his hands during Israel's battle
Leviticus 19:18 - Command to love your neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 17:11 - Moses holding up his hands during Israel's battle
questions.explanation: Exodus 17:11 shows Moses praying for God's presence in battle, paralleling Psalms 60:10's plea for God to not abandon the armies.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 60 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 60 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:1 suggest about God's relationship with His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:1 states, 'O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.' This indicates a moment of distress in the relationship.

questions.question: What hard experience is mentioned in Psalms 60:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:3 mentions, 'Thou hast shewed thy people hard things: thou hast made us to drink the wine of astonishment.' This references the difficult experiences faced by God's people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:4, what has God given to those who fear Him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:4 states, 'Thou hast given a banner to them that fear thee, that it may be displayed because of the truth.' This symbolizes God's protection and truth for His people.

questions.question: What does God's right hand represent in Psalms 60:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:5 says, 'That thy beloved may be delivered; save with thy right hand, and hear me.' This indicates the right hand symbolizes God's power to save.

questions.question: Who does God claim ownership of in Psalms 60:7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:7 states, 'Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine;' indicating God's sovereign claim over these regions.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:11 reveal about reliance on human help?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:11 states, 'Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.' This emphasizes the futility of relying solely on human assistance.

questions.question: What does Psalms 60:12 teach about victory through God?
options: Through God we shall do valiantly
questions.correctAnswer: Through God we shall do valiantly
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:12 states, 'Through God we shall do valiantly: for he it is that shall tread down our enemies.' It highlights reliance on divine strength for victory.

questions.question: What aspect of God's character is emphasized in Psalms 60:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:6 states, 'God hath spoken in his holiness...' which emphasizes God's pure and separate nature from sin.

questions.question: How does Psalms 60:8 characterize Moab and Edom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:8 says, 'Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe...' suggesting their lowly status in relation to God's people.

questions.question: What question is posed regarding entering the strong city in Psalms 60:9?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:9 asks, 'Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?' indicating a search for divine guidance.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the wine of astonishment' in Psalms 60:3 signify?
questions.explanation: The 'wine of astonishment' in Psalms 60:3 symbolizes the overwhelming and distressing experiences faced by the people.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5 and 12 convey about divine assistance?
options: God helps those who help themselves
Only God can deliver us from trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Only God can deliver us from trouble
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 12 emphasize reliance on God for deliverance and victory, indicating that true help comes from Him alone.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight emerges from Psalms 60:1 and 10 regarding God's presence in distress?
options: God does not care about our struggles
God is distant in times of trouble
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 10 express a sense of being cast off by God, highlighting a perceived absence in times of distress.

questions.question: According to Psalms 60:4 and 6, what is the purpose of God's banner?
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:4 states the banner is for those who fear God, emphasizing truth, while verse 6 points to rejoicing in God's promises.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that God does not provide for His people in times of trouble. What does Psalms 60:11-12 actually teach?
options: Divine help is essential for victory
God is indifferent to human struggles
questions.correctAnswer: Divine help is essential for victory
questions.explanation: Psalms 60:11-12 indicates that while human help is vain, true victory comes through God, affirming His provision.
